scope: Complete HBQ unstuckLoop admission, escalation and terminal cleanup compared with current WAIT ordinary recovery; not whole-mod parity

findings.evidence: After feature, alive crew, player crew and player leader checks, RouteLost runs before Loading, Blocked, ShouldMove and the physical stuck test. It can relocate and refresh a route despite Busy, Pause, loading, authored waypoint waits, disabled PATH or ASSAULT. Player visibility still blocks this fast path.
findings.disposition: Reject this bypass. All recovery paths must retain current task, mobility and controller admission before each movement mutation. WAIT ordinary recovery uses mayRecoverOrdinaryRoute and mayIssueDriving at command boundaries; no equivalent RouteLost shortcut is added.

findings.evidence: RouteLost increments TeleportsInRow on handled relocation, then continues before the normal delete/give-up threshold checks. Repeated RouteLost reports can therefore bypass those thresholds. It clears RouteLost before attempting both relocation helpers and refreshes the route even when both return false.
findings.disposition: Retain immediate diagnosis intent, not immediate relocation. A route fault must consume a durable finite episode and distinguish failed command issue from observed physical route progress.

findings.evidence: Step three increments TeleportsInRow regardless of helper result and can log relocation despite a failed fallback. Visible stuck vehicles cap StuckCount at two, repeating repair/nudge without reaching the teleport-count give-up branch.
findings.disposition: Do not import success counters or unlimited visible retries. WAIT retains durable EXHAUSTED stage, route receipts and measured progress; physical native reverse and jam resolution remain unaccepted.

findings.evidence: Base delay five uses multiplier twenty in COMBAT or two otherwise, then max fifteen plus three: 103 or 18 seconds before precision scaling [2,1.5,1]. Header low-precision multiplier is stale. RouteLost cuts the scheduled wait to approximately its one-second polling interval.
findings.disposition: Use executable cadence, not comments, for cost comparison. These intervals do not establish WAIT median or p95 overhead.

findings.evidence: Stuck is displacement below two metres, or below four with less than 2.5 metres improvement toward destination. Speed above three km/h exempts ordinary stuck, but ProgT older than ninety seconds overrides that exemption. Snapshot is not tied to an unchanged route or seat receipt.
findings.disposition: Separate oscillation, queue waiting, new authored orders and actual route progress. WAIT binds recovery to route and seat receipts; direct script-order recovery remains a separate unsupported case.

findings.evidence: Entry and loop require local vehicle, but terminal UnstuckRunning false write is outside the locality guard and has no generation comparison.
findings.disposition: Old-owner cleanup must not retire a replacement owner episode. WAIT recovery release compares current journal before clearing and admits only current local owner.

findings.evidence: Escalation calls the previously reviewed helper for forced nudge, optional mobility repair and relocation, and optionally deletes vehicle and crew.
findings.disposition: Reject these shortcuts for natural WAIT recovery. Useful intent is finite diagnosis, protected task admission, collision-aware native movement and explicit failure. No production shortcut or new physical acceptance is introduced.
